checks.title: 3. evaluate.py cannot produce the planned tests (no diffs against clock, no time-matched bootstrap, no (b) fairness columns, one-sided p, too few draws)
checks.evidence: L488 and L616 set the references for differences to ['pairwise','bag','bag+graph'] plus ext:*. In the committed oof/results.json and frozen/results.json, the only references in the paired diffs are ['bag','bag+graph','pairwise'] (c2_a_vs_b.py). There is a 'clock - pairwise' entry, but no 'zs:pairwise - clock' and no 'zs:global_full - zs:pairwise'. bootstrap() (L236-246) resamples only auroc and auprc. Time-matched, mixed and before_announcement AUROCs exist only in the (a) slices() output, as point estimates without CIs. The frozen split keys are ['metrics','paired_diffs','lead_time','run_level','node']. L255 gives a one-sided p_le_0 only. frozen() writes no row scores: only oof/preds.csv is written (L512), and report.py writes only RESULTS.md and figures. The plan asks for 1000 draws in §4, at least 2000 in §4b, and passes --boot 1000 in §5. The first Holm threshold for 11 tests is 0.05/11 = 0.0045. With 1,000 draws the two-sided p moves in steps of 0.002. With 2,000 draws the Monte-Carlo SE at p≈0.0045 is 2·sqrt(0.00225·0.99775/2000) ≈ 0.0021. The reviewer's phrase 'below the 0.002 step' is garbled, but the point stands. Family (b) (6 overall-AUROC tests, with ext:* as reference) is computable, but only one-sided; family (a), the time-matched tests against clock, is not computable at all.
checks.fix: Change evaluate.py and commit it before the plan. (1) bootstrap() gets an optional strata argument. In each draw it also computes stratified_auroc over the rounds_to_cut bins [-99,-9,-5,-1,3,99], and it returns p_two_sided = min(1, 2·min(P(d≤0), P(d≥0))). (2) The difference references become ['clock','pairwise','bag','bag+graph','zs:pairwise','zs:global_full'] plus ext:*. (3) frozen() adds a pooled held-out pseudo-split (test_id ∪ ood_family ∪ ood_seed), stores slices() per split, and writes frozen/preds.csv (episode_id, t, all scores). In the plan, use one number: 2,000 draws for all CIs (§4 and §5), and 10,000 draws for the primary Holm tests, run from frozen/preds.csv.

Its OOF uses GroupKFold over 112 configs; the harness uses folds.json (StratifiedGroupKFold over 64 configs). The two time-matching definitions differ: gnn_opt/metrics.py L34-43 uses round bins 1-5, 6-10, … weighted by positives; evaluate.py L93-103 and L262 use rounds-to-cut bins weighted by pairs. My script c6_timematch.py computes both on identical rows (harness ID-OOF repeat 0, 3,370 rows, 135 positives). hgb_clock: harness 0.424 vs llm_monitor 0.632. hgb_bag+graph: 0.773 vs 0.810. +mem: 0.800 vs 0.833. Define 'zeitgematcht' as llm_monitor.evaluate.stratified_auroc over the rounds_to_cut bins ≤−9, −8…−5, −4…−1, 0…3, >3, and name it explicitly. Declare the harness-row stage descriptive (all its inputs have been seen); if it is kept, take clock and bag+graph from the harness CV files of the same folds. Mark zs:*−bag+graph as not blinded. checks.title: 7. vx_shift does not resample with replacement and cannot test Δ_shift against Δ_noise
checks.evidence: L655-661 concatenate the row indices of the drawn bases and then write them into boolean masks (mA[ma] = True). A base drawn k times therefore counts once, and each draw is the union of about 14·(1−(13/14)^14) = 9.04 distinct bases. The draws sit inside the per-arm and per-predictor loops and use one rng in sequence. So the arms, the noise floor and the predictors are never resampled on shared draws, and there is no CI for Δ_shift−Δ_noise or for Δ(GNN)−Δ(bag). Only AUROC is computed, and the output keys are just ['delta_auroc','ci','n_bases']. My script c1_c7_eval_paths.py runs the real E.vx_shift on 6 synthetic datasets with 14 bases and compares it to a proper cluster bootstrap with replacement. The CI width ratios are 0.79, 0.86, 0.76, 0.72, 0.80 and 0.76 (mean 0.78); theory predicts about 0.77. The CIs are therefore about 20 % too narrow. §6 promises time-matched and AUPRC deltas for glm, which the code does not produce.
checks.fix: Rewrite vx_shift. For each arm (excluding id, rep, ft4, b4 and bal), use the bases that have the arm, id rep0 and id rep1. Draw once per arm `[rng.choice(bases, len(bases), replace=True) for _ in range(B)]` and share these draws across all predictors. Inside a draw, use concatenated index arrays rather than masks, so repeated bases count repeatedly. Report delta_shift = A−I0, delta_noise = I1−I0 and shift_minus_noise = A−I1, with percentile CIs from the same draws, for AUROC, AUPRC and time-matched AUROC. Add paired Δ differences between predictors (ext:gnn_final − bag, ext:gnn_final − pairwise). Plan §6 should then read: H2 and H4 are decided by the CI of A−I1, H3 and H5 by the CI of Δ(GNN)−Δ(bag).

checks.title: 8. The plan says it adopts VALIDATION.md §3 but departs from §3.1-§3.3 and HARNESS.md without saying so
checks.evidence: VALIDATION.md L177-178 selects by grouped 5-fold CV over the 76 train+val configs, using OOF AUPRC. The GNN was selected by the harness score on 64 night_train configs (HARNESS.md §2). Plan §5's last paragraph mentions this, but not as a departure. L180-181 says 'evaluate test_* and night_vx_* once'; (b) has been run 7 times for the LLM monitors and references (check 4). In evaluate.py the refits at L587 and L604 use a single seed of 0, and L582 fixes EdgeMonitor(E, 0). In sklearn 1.9.1, early stopping is on only when n > 10,000, so HGB and LR on the 4,050 pool rows are deterministic, but the EdgeMonitor (trained on edge rows) is not. HARNESS.md §2/§3 says to train only on night_train, and the eval file comes from all night_train rows. finalize.py L73 and L84 store trained_on 'night_train (all 128 runs)', and train.py L39 hard-codes TRAIN_SPLIT = 'night_train', so the planned train+val retrain needs a code change and a new run. VALIDATION §3.2 and §3.3 (L183-206) ask for K0, structure-only, node level and risk_count MAE. evaluate.py L173 reads only p_graph, so the GNN gets none of these. §3.5 (L223-228) says 'GNN', 'bag' and 'pairwise' without defining which GNN.
checks.fix: Replace plan line 8 with an explicit list of deviations. (1) GNN selection uses the harness score on 64 night_train configs, not OOF AUPRC on train+val. (2) The LLM monitors and references were evaluated on the test splits several times; 'einmal' now holds only for the GNN and night_vx. (3) References and heads are refit with one seed (deterministic for HGB/LR here). (4) The final GNN is retrained on train+val, unlike HARNESS.md §2/§3; this needs a TRAIN_SPLIT change and a new training run, and models/final.pt is trained on train only. (5) K0, structure-only, node level and the GNN's risk_count MAE run in the harness, not in llm_monitor.evaluate. (6) In H1-H5, 'GNN' means ext:gnn_final, and 'bag' and 'pairwise' are the llm_monitor references of the same names.

checks.title: 10. The primary GNN tests compare against the weaker tabular model (bag+graph, without per-agent memory)
checks.evidence: gnn_opt_torch/RESULTS.md L24 and L35 say the strongest headline-compliant tabular baseline is hgb_bag+graph+mem (select 0.848), while hgb_bag+graph (0.834) is 'the named reference'. L153 gives final GNN − hgb_bag+graph = +0.035 [−0.003, +0.083] and final GNN − hgb_bag+graph+mem = +0.014 [−0.031, +0.060]. The 'Honest verdict' there says the GNN alone (0.839) does not beat +mem (0.848). The hybrid is final + hgb_bag+graph+mem, so gnn_hybrid − bag+graph mixes the GNN effect with the memory-feature effect. gnn_opt/tabular.py L81 defines memory_feats, which are causal per-agent memory features. llm_monitor refbase.feature_sets builds bag+graph from bag, g_* and d3_g_* only, with no memory features. On identical rows (c6_timematch.py) hgb_bag+graph has AUROC 0.849 and +mem 0.871. FINDINGS §4 (L80-81) credits per-agent memory for the GNN's transfer. Nuance: VALIDATION §3.2 lists 'bag + graph aggregates' as the predictor, so this is a weak choice of comparator for RQ3 rather than a code error.
